description: Evidence-backed current product specifications, baseline drift, incremental reconciliation, optional shipped evidence, and boundaries against future planning or code work

prompts.prompt: reverse engineer my current app into a PRD and compare it against the original
expected_behaviors: Find and preserve the original intent with provenance before comparison
Reconstruct current product behavior rather than invent future requirements
Determine whether repository source is sufficient before considering reverse-engineer-anything
prompts.boundary: PRD and reverse engineer describe an existing product reconciliation, not future planning or an automatic artifact-analysis trigger

prompts.prompt: our docs are stale, tell me what the product has actually become
expected_behaviors: Describe user-visible capabilities and product contracts with evidence
Keep baseline intent separate from the current as-built specification

prompts.prompt: update the as-built spec from everything changed since the last reconciliation
expected_behaviors: Read the saved reconciliation checkpoint and inspect its Git range through HEAD
Map changed files to affected product areas and preserve unrelated verified records
Advance the checkpoint only for a completed reconciliation scope

prompts.prompt: compare the current authentication behavior with the original requirements and write the product changelog
expected_behaviors: Compare intended and observed authentication contracts
Record product evolution separately from repository release notes
Cite evidence for what changed, when it changed, and any established reason

prompts.prompt: we inherited this shipped Electron app and need an evidence-backed current spec
expected_behaviors: Establish source availability and identify claims dependent on the shipped package
Use reverse-engineer-anything for required shipped evidence and preserve its evidence limits
Do not treat a source checkout as proof of an unverified shipped version

prompts.prompt: Reverse engineer my app into an as-built PRD. The complete source and tests are here, and all the behavior we need to document can be established from them.
expected_behaviors: Use focused source and test evidence with the normal code-intelligence path
Skip reverse-engineer-anything because source evidence is sufficient
Do not invoke artifact tooling merely because the user said reverse engineer

prompts.prompt: Reconcile this source repository with its old PRD. SymDex and REA are not installed, but the source and tests are complete.
expected_behaviors: Continue using bounded repository search and focused file reads through the source fallback
Do not block source-only reconciliation on an optional child
Do not silently install tools or modify the environment

prompts.prompt: The checked-in login code allows passwords, but our shipped desktop app only offers magic links. Reconcile its actual product specification against the old PRD.
expected_behaviors: Separate source behavior from versioned shipped or runtime observations
Use reverse-engineer-anything for claims that require the shipped application
Keep unresolved contradictions explicit instead of forcing a single authoritative answer

prompts.prompt: We only have an APK and the original requirements. Build a current product spec and drift report; REA's skill is present but its MCP tools are not connected.
expected_behaviors: Load reverse-engineer-anything for the artifact-dependent work and follow its own connection and recovery contract
Distinguish installed skill instructions from available MCP tooling
Preserve baseline work and mark artifact claims unverified while the required evidence is blocked
Do not silently install analysis engines or invent APK behavior

prompts.prompt: The old PRD says passwords, current code uses magic links, and the commit only says 'auth cleanup'. Explain why the product changed in the drift report.
expected_behaviors: Record the observed authentication change with evidence
Record its reason as unknown because an implementation change and vague commit message do not establish intent
Separate observed fact, inferred intent, and unknown without inventing a security or conversion rationale

prompts.prompt: Reconcile the current app against our original product intent. README, docs/PRD.md, and an accepted ADR disagree about whether guests may export reports.
expected_behaviors: Record each baseline candidate and its provenance instead of assuming README is authoritative
Resolve authority from evidence or preserve the baseline ambiguity
Keep guest-export behavior and the reason for the intended policy separately evidenced

prompts.prompt: Update our living specification after the new onboarding shipped. Keep the original PRD intact so we can still see what drifted.
expected_behaviors: Preserve the original baseline snapshot and provenance
Update the current specification, drift ledger, and product evolution history
Do not rewrite original intent merely to match current behavior

prompts.prompt: Create an as-built specification for the app we inherited. There is no original PRD and we have not found any requirements or roadmap.
expected_behaviors: Document evidenced current product contracts without manufacturing an original baseline
Mark baseline and intent as unknown where no evidence exists
Do not classify every existing capability as an intentional addition to an invented baseline

prompts.prompt: Only billing files changed since the last spec reconciliation. Update the current product spec and explain any billing drift without rescanning all the unrelated features.
expected_behaviors: Use the saved Git checkpoint and changed paths to identify affected contracts
Revalidate billing and any demonstrated shared dependencies
Carry forward unaffected areas with their original evidence freshness rather than pretending they were rechecked

prompts.prompt: Reconcile this exported source folder with the previous as-built spec. It has no .git directory, so we cannot compute the last-reconciled-commit range.
expected_behaviors: Use available snapshots or fingerprints to bound changes when possible
Explicitly widen the reconciliation if a reliable incremental range cannot be established
Leave unavailable introduction commits and historical reasons unknown

prompts.prompt: Update the living product spec, but the saved reconciliation commit disappeared after a history rewrite. Do not pretend the old checkpoint is still valid.
expected_behaviors: Validate checkpoint availability and ancestry before using a Git range
Record the history discontinuity and deliberately rebuild or widen the affected scope
Preserve baseline provenance and never run destructive Git recovery

prompts.prompt: Reconcile the app's current behavior with the PRD, including my uncommitted changes, and make the evidence clear about what has and has not been committed.
expected_behaviors: Identify the working-tree scope and distinguish dirty-file evidence from committed HEAD
Keep the incremental checkpoint truthful so uncommitted changes cannot disappear from the next reconciliation
Do not commit application changes or silently edit the app during reconciliation

prompts.prompt: The old PRD promises CSV export. Its implementation still exists behind a permanently disabled feature flag. Record this accurately in the current spec and drift report.
expected_behaviors: Distinguish dormant implementation from a currently available user capability
Cite flag and reachability evidence rather than treating code existence as proof of availability
Do not enable the feature to erase the drift

prompts.prompt: Tests say free accounts can export, source denies it, and nobody has checked the deployed version. Reconcile that requirement in our product specification.
expected_behaviors: Record conflicting source and test evidence with their scope and revision
Do not claim production behavior without production evidence
Mark unresolved current claims unverified and use the shipped-evidence gate only for claims that require it

prompts.prompt: Compare the current report-retention behavior with the old PRD. ADR-014 explicitly approved reducing retention to 30 days; Git shows the implementing commit a week later.
expected_behaviors: Use the ADR as intent evidence and the implementation commit as change evidence
Keep decision time, implementation time, and observed release scope distinct
Cite both sources in the product evolution record

prompts.prompt: Write a PRD for a feature we haven't built yet.
prompts.boundary: new intended behavior belongs to plan; PRD alone does not select spec

prompts.prompt: Create a PRD for a new referrals feature before we start implementation.
Explain how authentication works in this repo.
prompts.boundary: code understanding without a specification, baseline comparison, or evolution deliverable

prompts.prompt: Reverse engineer the request flow in this complete source repo: show me the entry points and callers. I only need a code walkthrough.
expected_behaviors: Use source navigation rather than automatic artifact analysis
Do not manufacture a living-specification task from the phrase reverse engineer
prompts.boundary: reverse engineer is colloquial source exploration, not product reconciliation

prompts.prompt: Review this PR.
prompts.boundary: judge a proposed code change rather than reconstruct current product contracts

prompts.prompt: Review the authentication diff for bugs and maintainability before I merge it.
prompts.boundary: authentication is the review subject, not a specification reconciliation request

prompts.prompt: Implement the missing PRD requirement now: change the known report export limit from 20 to 50 and run its existing test.
prompts.boundary: known scoped implementation belongs to ship even though a PRD supplies the requirement

prompts.prompt: Refactor the billing module into smaller modules without changing behavior.
prompts.boundary: structure-only implementation work does not require a product-specification pass

prompts.prompt: Reconcile the existing app against the original PRD, then plan which missing requirements we should build next. Do not implement anything yet.
expected_behaviors: Complete current-reality reconciliation before planning future decisions
Pass unresolved requirements and evidence to plan with one router active at a time
Do not silently implement discovered drift
prompts.boundary: explicit reconciliation followed by future planning warrants a two-router handoff

prompts.prompt: Ship the known one-line export limit fix, then reconcile the living product spec and product changelog with the implemented behavior.
expected_behaviors: Implement and verify the scoped fix before handing completed behavior to spec
Reconcile only because the user explicitly requested that follow-up
prompts.boundary: spec is an explicit post-implementation job, not an automatic step in every ship request

prompts.prompt: Plan the requirements for a small new report-retention rule, implement the agreed rule, and then reconcile our as-built spec against that approved intent.
expected_behaviors: Resolve intended behavior before implementation
Respect the plan approval boundary before activating ship
After implementation, reconcile the current spec with the preserved intent using at most three routers
prompts.boundary: explicit intent, implementation, and reconciliation compose a three-step plan; no companion becomes a chain step

prompts.prompt: Use reverse-engineer-anything to decompile this native executable and identify its serialization routine. I do not want a product specification.
expected_behaviors: Keep the explicitly requested low-level reverse-engineering task with reverse-engineer-anything
Do not hijack it into routr-spec or treat REA as a routr domain selector
prompts.boundary: behavior-only case: the router-selection scorer has no no-router or direct-child outcome
